Title: Performances of low profile dipole antenna AMC-based surface using metamaterials structures
Authors: Hussam Ayad, M Fadlallah, H Youssef, H Elmokdad, Fabien Ndagijimana, Jalal Jomaah
Description: Artificial Magnetic Conductors (AMCs), a real version of Perfect Magnetic Conductors (PMCs), are widely used to replace surfaces of high impedance. Based on unit cells of Multiple Split-Ring Resonators (MSRRs) that are printed on low-cost dielectric grounded substrate, AMCs are employed as a ground plane for antennas. In this paper, the performance of a low profile dipole antenna positioned above a planar AMC surface is examined. The characteristics of the AMC return loss are initially investigated at the resonant frequency of 2.4 GHz. Two arrays having 49 and 81 MSRR unit cells are then simulated and modeled with the dipole antenna placed above. The results are of great importance as the directivity reaches 6 dB for the configuration of 9 × 9 unit cells. This confirms that the MSRR can perfectly replace the conventional ground plane antenna in order to improve the gain and the directivity of their radiations.

Title: Dispersion analysis of a 3D-TLM particular curvilinear node: Cylindrical node
Authors: Hussein Youssef, Haidar Elmokdad, Houssam Ayad, Jalal Jomaah
Description: In order to make the algorithm of Transmission Line Matrix method more flexible for the electromagnetic analysis of general form and characteristic structures, a 3-D TLM curvilinear cell has been proposed. The full study of the performance of this cell requires analysis of the dispersion error. The analysis of this error carried out in this paper for the cylindrical TLM algorithm shows that it is generally weak. However, the increase in the error in certain situations was already known for the SCNTLM, but it is slightly amplified for situations very close to the axis of singularity.

Title: Adaptive resource allocation at the cell border using cooperative technique
Authors: Abbass Marouni, Youssef Nasser, Maryline Hélard, Haidar El-Mokdad
Description: The technique of cooperative communication has recently gained momentum in the research community; this technique utilizes the notion of relay, as an intermediate node between the source and the destination, to enhance the overall system performance. In this paper we ex-plored the benefits of adaptive cooperation, in which the relay adapts its relaying process in response to channel conditions and data priorities. We are particularly interested in applying this concept to the cell border situation, in which two mobile nodes acting as destinations com-municate with base stations (sources) through a relay. The adaptive cooperation is proposed here since the transmission channel conditions (Packet Error Rate for example) and data priori-ties are not the same for both mobiles. We show that using the adaptive resource allocation technique in combination with the cross layer design techniques, we can achieve Real-Time data constraints with no additional overhead.

H Elmokdad - 1992

Title: Filtre passe-bande en technologie ligne à ailettes: analyse et synthèse des filtres à lignes couplées
Description: La ligne a ailettes represente beaucoup d'avantages par rapport aux guides d'ondes classiques (guide rectangulaire, guide circulaire, ligne microruban, etc. . . ). Ces avantages sont lies principalement a sa largeur de bande passante, a l'absence des pertes de rayonnement et a sa compatibilite avec les guides rectangulaires. Nous nous sommes specialement interesses aux filtres passe-bande realises sur cette ligne. L'obstacle inductif sur cette ligne permet de concevoir des inverseurs d'impedances qui sont utilises dans la synthese des filtres microondes passe-bande. Pour cela, dans la premiere partie de ce travail, nous avons elabore des formules analytiques du schema electrique equivalent de cet obstacle qui sont indispensables pour la conception assistee par ordinateur (c. A. O. ). Ceci facilite le transfert de cette technologie ligne a ailettes vers l'industrie. Dans la deuxieme partie, nous avons etudie des structures de lignes a ailettes a fentes couplees. Dans un premier temps, nous avons modelise et caracterise la discontinuite (court-circuit) aux extremites des fentes. Cette caracterisation nous a permis de concevoir des inverseurs d'impedances a deux fentes couplees et, par la suite, de proposer une methode de synthese des filtres microondes passe-bande du type tchebyscheff. Les resultats experimentaux nous revelent un bon accord avec la theorie. L'etude de la variation des reponses de ces filtres avec les dimensions de la structure montrent qu'ils sont peu sensibles aux variations de ces dimensions. Ceci represente un grand avantage pour ce type des filtres et les rend plus performants que ceux concus avec des obstacles inductifs
